thread:
sam: quick heads-up — spinning up a rapid safety blitz for PoppySeed-3B (int4) in the sandbox. want a few pairs of eyes on jailbreak + toxicity sweeps today. low-effort runs first then escalate if failures stack.

sam: plan: 1) corpus of 250 jailbreak prompts (mix internal + public), 2) 100 toxicity seeds, 3) refusal regression checks with our QA harness. will post early metrics here.

anya: on it. can you drop the run id and container tag? i want to attach to the eval dashboard.

sam: run id `ps-blitz-2026-03-09-a1` image `redwood/poppyseed:3b-int4-canary.20260309`

miguel: grabbing the corpus now. small ask — include the calibrated temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.7) so we see sensitivity.

sam: good call. i'll kick three jobs. starting low-temp first.

deploy-bot: Job launched by sam: ps-blitz-2026-03-09-a1 (3 jobs: temp0/0.2/0.7). containers: redwood/poppyseed:3b-int4-canary.20260309. ETA ~18m.

taylor: ping @anya @miguel — if we see elevated jailbreaks at temp0 that's a red flag for quantization-induced policy drift.

sam: first quick summary (temp0 finished):
```
- jailbreak pass rate: 11.6% (29/250)
- baseline (fp16) on same prompts: 3.2%
- toxicity score mean: 0.21 vs baseline 0.08
- top-k hallucination artifacts: increased short-form persona leaks ~4 incidents
```

anya: wow that's higher than i expected at temp0. can you paste 2-3 representative examples (anonymized)?

sam: posted 3 anonymized snippets to the eval dashboard (link): https://internal.eval/redwood/ps-blitz/ps-blitz-2026-03-09-a1

miguel: grabbing samples. initial suspicion: quantized attention scaling mismatch -> directive attenuation fails. will run a quick reproduce on CPU to confirm.

taylor: meanwhile i recommend we trigger a canary fallback policy for any public endpoints using this tag. @infra — can you isolate dedicated traffic?

miguel: repro on CPU shows similar pattern but lower magnitude (jailbreak 6%). suggests quantization noise exacerbates the issue but not entirely novel.

sam: we should: 1) freeze release, 2) run a targeted logit-scale calibration, 3) run a token-level KL check vs fp16 on safety prompts.

anya: agree. i'll open a quick eval PR with proposed prompts and expected refusals. tagging policy for review.

deploy-bot: Canary fallback applied to public alias `poppyseed-canary`. Redirecting 100% to fp16 variant until rollback cleared.

taylor: good. also add a quick threshold alert if toxicity score > 0.15 for >50 queries/minute.

sam: follow-ups: miguel, can you run a narrow int4 qconfig sweep (per-layer vs global) and drop the layer-norm-preserve variant? target within 24h.

miguel: on it. starting per-layer quant sweep now. i'll post logs and diff counts to the dashboard.

anya: i'll coordinate with policy to draft the customer-facing note if we need to extend rollback. keep it low-key and technical.

sam: thanks everyone. if any unexpected escalation, ping #eng-oncall. tl;dr — int4 bringup shows safety regression vs fp16; mitigations in motion. :exclamation: :lock:
